Cautiously positive and consistent with the literature: the FOMC notes strengthening activity and employment while beginning a measured taper of QE and maintaining rates at 0–0.25%. This mix aligns with research on unconventional policy—QE and forward guidance work primarily through long-term rates and term premia (e.g., the Fed’s QE/forward-guidance toolkit; Cochrane–Piazzesi on the term structure), so gradual tapering alongside accommodative guidance can keep financial conditions easy even as asset purchases decline. The commitment to let inflation run moderately above 2% to achieve an average 2% is in the spirit of inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson and Woodford), aiming to anchor expectations and mitigate average inflation bias through credible commitment. At the same time, the statement’s emphasis on supply–demand imbalances and pandemic-related constraints fits cost-push dynamics in New Keynesian models (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans; Ravenna and Walsh), where inflation can be transitory if expectations remain anchored. Finally, the conditional language about “adjusting the pace” and “risks to the outlook” acknowledges the Taylor principle (Clarida/Taylor rule): if elevated inflation persists or expectations drift, policy must respond more than one-for-one, tempering excessive optimism. Overall tone: slightly positive but risk-aware.
